taxonomy.subtopic: Synovial pannus, RANKL signaling, and marginal erosions

questions.stem_html:
A 46-year-old woman has 8 months of symmetric pain and swelling in the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. Morning stiffness lasts 2 hours. Examination shows boggy synovitis, and radiographs reveal periarticular osteopenia and marginal erosions. Synovial biopsy demonstrates proliferative granulation tissue extending over articular cartilage.

Which process most directly produces the marginal bone erosions?

options.text_html: Deposition of monosodium urate crystals directly dissolves subchondral bone
Loss of chondrocyte proteoglycan synthesis alone creates osteophytes
Immune-complex occlusion of nutrient arteries causes avascular necrosis
Calcification of articular cartilage activates neutrophils within the meniscus
RANKL expression by activated synovial cells and T cells stimulates osteoclast differentiation

questions.explanation_html: Inflamed synovium forms pannus. Cytokines such as TNF and IL-1 promote RANKL expression, which drives osteoclast formation and focal bone erosion at joint margins. RANKL-mediated osteoclast activation is the direct link between chronic synovitis and erosive bone loss in rheumatoid arthritis.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Urate crystals cause gouty erosions with a different distribution and histology.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: This describes degenerative osteoarthritis rather than inflammatory marginal erosions.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Avascular necrosis is not the typical mechanism of rheumatoid marginal erosions.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition causes pseudogout and chondrocalcinosis, not rheumatoid pannus.

questions.educational_objective: Connect rheumatoid pannus and inflammatory cytokines to RANKL-dependent osteoclast activation and marginal erosions.
